## Summary

Answered a fair challenge: the protocol-block gap found last turn had NOT been made a task. It was recorded as repo memory and in a commit body, then flagged as "worth deciding" in a wrap-up and left there — which is exactly how work gets lost, and precisely the failure this initiative exists to catch. Fixed by opening session-orientation rather than bloating this record, since commit-attribution is about binding commits and reviewing execution while the new one is about how a session picks its record. It carries 8 tasks across 3 phases: teaching re-homing in both shipped protocol dialects (including that protocol blocks are VERSIONED, so 1.1 must append a new shipped version rather than edit in place), deciding whether end_session should be targetable at all against record-integrity D13's ban on session splits, and orienting a fresh session on a bound branch with the tension stated plainly — "last worked" is global and can be a peer's work, so silently loading it would recreate the misrouting class record-integrity fixed. Its note records that the MECHANISM is correct and must not be rebuilt; only the telling side is missing.

## Next action

Build 3.4, the ref-gated UserPromptSubmit line that tells a LIVE session its commits reached origin — the floor D13's optional ping layers onto. Also open here: 2.3 squash-merge recovery, all of Phase 5, and docs/SPEC.md (5.4). Session-orientation now tracks the re-homing and fresh-session gaps separately, starting at its 1.1.
